evidence.reason: The duplicate branch is explicitly documented as intentional: the comment at lines 183-186 states 'IDs remain sticky, including already-terminal items.' A terminal item sharing the exact push id means that identical range (reviewed..tip) was already completed, or was itself coalesced into a covering item — in this code the only way an item becomes terminal-'skipped' is via the coalesce branch (line 179), which records the successor id in its note. So the duplicate check firing means the exact range is already covered or deliberately superseded, and declining to re-enroll the same id is a deliberate dedupe that avoids duplicate reviews, not an oversight. The finding's loss scenario requires a contrived state (a terminal item whose id equals the current reviewed..tip pair, simultaneously with an unrelated pending range, plus a branch reset/force-push that drops the covering item) that is not established by the supplied code, and the proposed reordering would change the documented sticky-ID/dedupe behavior and could cause redundant reviews of already-covered ranges. That is a hardening/behavior-change proposal against intentional, commented implementation, not a demonstrable current defect; any such change would need owner judgment on review-cost tradeoffs.
